description: Aggregate-mapped apply lowering gate: every binding loads tests/conformance/reprojection/lcc_grid_roundtrip/fixture.esm -- a model whose observed fields invoke the reprojection/lambert_conformal.esm templates INSIDE aggregate exprs, with per-site bindings mixing indexed reads ({op: index, args: [x_grid, i, j]}), numeric literals (lat_1=30, lat_2=60, lat_0=40, lon_0=-97), and a variable name reference (R bound to R_sphere) -- runs the raw section-9.7 pipeline (import resolution, section-9.7.3 registration-time helper composition of the library's _t/_n/_F/_rho/_theta fragments, section-9.6.2/9.6.4 Option A expansion), and must emit a byte-identical expanded AST: every apply_expression_template inlined into a closed scalar expression over the evaluable core at each aggregate site, the aggregate/index scaffolding and the i/j index symbols inside the substituted subtrees intact, zero unlowered rewrite-target ops. This is the five-way byte pin for the one 9.6.2 lowering path the scalar-point reprojection harness (runner-built wrapper docs, scalar parameter variables) does not cover: expansion of a template invocation whose bindings reference the enclosing aggregate's index symbols. The golden is generated by the Julia reference runner only (scripts/regenerate-goldens.sh) and compared bytewise by the other bindings. AUTHORING CONSTRAINT carried by the fixture: its non-integral decimal literals are kept to <= 15 significant digits because the Rust binding's JSON float fast path parses some 16-17-digit decimals 1 ulp off (observed on -104.52369275835723 and 42.059133583516356), which shifts the re-emitted shortest-digits token and breaks byte identity; the template library's own inlined radian-degree constants (17 digits) happen to parse exactly and round-trip byte-identically through all five bindings.
